narrative.title: The Fleet-Wide Charter Quota
narrative.scenario: The regulator now issues the broker a quota of k lock-release cycles per quarter. The fleet's scheduling terminal must allocate those k cycles across the fee curve to harvest the largest combined spread, never overlapping two cycles. When the quota exceeds the number of profitable swings, the cap effectively disappears.
narrative.inputFormat: An integer k and an array prices where prices[i] is the fee on hour i.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the maximum profit using at most k non-overlapping buy-sell transactions.

testCases.explanation: The only climb is 2 to 4; one cycle captures it all.
(2 to 6) plus (0 to 3) — both cycles inside the quota.

hintLevels: Level 1: Same machine as the two-cycle version, with the cap as a parameter instead of a constant.
Level 2: dp[day][holding][cycles-used]; a buy increments the cycle count and hitting k seals the machine shut.
Level 3: When k >= n/2 the cap can never bind — fall back to the unlimited-trades answer to stay fast.
